BILL NUMBER:  S5921

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the education law, in relation to the registration of
entities providing certain professional services and the licensure of
certain professionals; to amend chapter 420 of the laws of 2002,
amending the education law relating to the profession of social work,
in relation to the effect of such provisions on certain governmental
entities and the effectiveness thereof; and to amend chapter 676 of
the laws of 2002, amending the education law relating to mental health
care practitioners, in relation to the effect of such provisions on
certain governmental entities and the effectiveness thereof


 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :

The purpose of this bill is to prevent the disruption of services to
the public in the professions of licensed master social work, licensed
clinical social work, licensed mental health counseling, licensed
marriage and family therapy, licensed creative arts therapy, licensed
psychoanalysis, and licensed psychology by creating an exemption from
corporate practice prohibitions for not-for-profit corporations,.
education corporations, firms, business corporations, and other
business entities that provide professional services in these
professions, provided that the entities register with the State
Education Department ("Department") by July 1, 2011. Upon such
registration, the bill would permit such entities to employ licensed
professionals or contract with professional business entities to
provide such professional services. Additionally, the bill would
recognize work experience gained by individuals employed by such
entities and would permit such individuals to apply this experience
towards the experience qualifications for professional licensure.

 SUMMARY OF THE PROVISIONS OF THE BILL :

Section 1 of the bill would set forth the legislative intent of the
bill.

Section 2 of the bill would add a new §6503-a to Title VIII of the
Education Law to allow the Department to authorize not-for-profit
corporations, education corporations, firms, business corporations and
other business entities that offer services provided by professionals
licensed under Education Law Article 154 (social work) Or Article 163
(mental health practitioners) of the Education Law or services
constituting the provision of psychotherapy as defined in Education
Law §8401(2) and authorized and provided under Education Law Article
131 (medicine), 139 (nursing) or 153 (psychology) and that are not
otherwise authorized by law to provide such professional services, to
provide these professional services upon registering with the
Department by July 1, 2011. New §6503-a would provide that any such
entity offering such professional services on this bill's effective
date would be deemed registered by the Department until submission of
an application for registration to the Department or until 120 days
after the Department prescribes an application form, whichever is
earlier. Upon its submission of such application, the entity would be
considered registered by the Department and would continue to be
considered registered unless and until its application is denied.
Notably, §6503-a would clarify that certain business entities would
not be required to register under the section, including (1)
appropriately organized professional business entities established
under the Business Corporation Law, the Limited Liability Company Law
or the Partnership Law, (2) certain entities operated by New York
State or federal agencies, political subdivisions, municipal
corporations, or local government agencies or units, (3) entities
operated under properly issued operating certificates, (4) a
university faculty practice corporation established under the
Not-for-Profit Corporation Law, (5) institutions of higher education
authorized to offer programs leading to licensure in the affected
professions that provide services as part of a registered program, and
(6) institutions of higher education that provide counseling to
students or staff and their families.

New §6503-a would require the entity to submit an application for
registration, as prescribed by the Commissioner of Education, and pay
an initial registration fee of $400.00 and a triennial registration
fee of $150.00 thereafter. Upon registration, the entity would be
required to disclose the scope of its practice, the names of its
owners, operators, directors, shareholder and officers, a listing of
any other jurisdiction in which it intends to provide services, and a
list of the professions under Title VIII of the Education Law in which
it intends to employ licensees. The application would include an
attestation which would include a statement that, unless otherwise
authorized by law, the entity will only provide professional services
authorized under §6503-a and any service appropriately related
thereto, as determined by the Department, and that only licensed
professionals or persons otherwise authorized to practice such
services, or professional business entities authorized by law to
provide such services will provide the professional services as
authorized under this section.

Additionally, each shareholder, director, officer, owner, member and
partner of the registering entity would be required to provide an
attestation regarding his or her moral character, which would include
a statement disclosing any criminal convictions, pending criminal
charges, determinations of professional misconduct, pending charges of
professional misconduct, or any limitations on professional practice.
Under §6503-a, these entities would be supervised by the Regents of
the University of the State of New York and would be subject to
disciplinary action to the same extent as professionals licensed under
Title VIII of the Education Law, including revocation, suspension and
annulment.

Sections 3, 4 and 5 of the bill would add new subdivision 8 to §6527
(medicine), new paragraph h to subdivision 1 to §6908 (nursing), and
new subdivision 9 to §7605 (psychology), respectively, to provide that
so long as an entity is registered under new §6503-a of the Education
Law, it may provide psychotherapy services (as defined in Education
Law §8401) to the extent permissible within the applicable scope of
professional practice by either a physician, nurse, or psychologist,
respectively, provided such services are provided through such an
appropriately licensed professional, or a professional business entity
authorized to provide such services.

Section 6 of the bill would add a new subdivision 6 to §7706 of the
Education Law to specifically permit any not-for-profit corporation,
education corporation, firm, business corporation, or other lawful
business entity registered with the Department pursuant to Education
Law §6503-a to provide licensed master social work and licensed
clinical social work services, provided such services are provided by
individuals appropriately licensed or otherwise authorized to provide
such services or by an authorized professional business entity.

Section 7 of the bill would add a new subdivision 7 to §8410 of the
Education Law to specifically permit any not-for-profit corporation,
education corporation, firm, business corporation, or other lawful
business entity registered with the Department pursuant to Education
Law §6503-a to provide mental health practitioner services, provided
such services are provided by individuals appropriately licensed or
otherwise authorized to provide such services or by an authorized
professional business entity.

Section 8 of the bill would amend subdivision 3 of §7603 of the
Education Law to provide that work experience in psychology gained in
a setting of an entity registered pursuant to §6503-a of the Education
Law may be applied towards the experience qualifications required by
the Department for professional licensure as a psychologist,
notwithstanding that such experience may have been obtained prior to
the effective date of §6503-a and/or prior to the registration of the
setting. Education Law §7603(3), as amended, would provide that the
Department may, for good cause, accept satisfactory experience
obtained in such a setting which would have been eligible for
registration but which has not yet registered with the Department or
experience that was obtained in good faith by the applicant under the
belief that appropriate authorization had been obtained.

Section 9 of the bill would amend paragraph c of subdivision 2 of
§7704 of the Education Law to provide that work experience in social
work gained in a setting of an entity registered pursuant to §6503-a
of the Education Law would may be applied towards the experience
qualifications required by the Department for professional licensure
as a social worker, notwithstanding that such experience may have been
obtained prior to the effective date of §6503-a and/or prior to the
registration of the setting. Education Law §7704(2)(c), as amended,
would provide that the Department may, for good cause, accept
satisfactory experience obtained in such a setting which would have
been eligible for registration but which has not yet registered with
the Department or experience that was obtained in good faith by the
applicant under the belief that appropriate authorization had been
obtained.

Section 10 of the bill would similarly amend paragraph c of
subdivision 3 of §8402 of the Education Law to provide that experience
in mental health counseling gained in a setting of an entity
registered pursuant to §6503-a of the Education Law may be applied
towards the experience qualifications required by the Department for
the licensure of an individual as a mental health practitioner,
notwithstanding that such experience may have been obtained prior to
the effective date of §6503-a and/or prior to the registration of the
setting. Education Law §8402(3)(c), as amended, would provide that the
Department may, for good cause, accept satisfactory experience
obtained in such setting that would have been eligible for
registration but which has not yet registered with the Department or
experience that was obtained in good faith by the applicant under the
belief that appropriate authorization had been obtained.

Section 11 of the bill would amend paragraph c of subdivision 3 of
§8403 of the Education Law to provide that experience in marriage and
family therapy gained in an entity registered pursuant to §6503-a of
the Education Law may be applied towards the experience qualifications
required by the Department for such professional licensure,
notwithstanding that such experience may have been obtained prior to
the effective date of §6503-a and/or prior to the registration of the
setting. Education Law §8403(3)(c), as amended, would provide that the
Department may, for good cause, accept satisfactory experience
obtained in a setting that would have been eligible for registration
but which has not registered with the Department or experience that
was obtained in good faith by the applicant under the belief that
appropriate authorization had been obtained.

Section 12 of the bill would amend paragraph c of subdivision 3 of
§8404 of the Education Law to provide that experience in creative arts
therapy gained in an entity registered pursuant to new Education Law
§6503-a may be applied towards the experience qualifications required
by the Department for such professional licensure, notwithstanding
that such experience may have been obtained prior to the effective
date of §6503-a and/or prior to the registration of the setting.
Education Law §8404(3)(c), as amended, would provide that the
Department may, for good cause, accept satisfactory experience
obtained in a setting that would have been eligible for registration
but which has not registered with the Department or experience that
was obtained in good faith by the applicant under the belief that
appropriate authorization had been obtained.

Section 13 of the bill would amend paragraph c of subdivision 3 of
§8405 of the Education Law to provide that experience in
psychoanalysis gained in an entity registered pursuant to new
Education Law §6503-a may be applied towards the experience
qualifications required by the Department for such professional
licensure, notwithstanding that such experience may have been obtained
prior to the effective date of §6503-a and/or prior to the
registration of the setting. Education Law §8405(3)(c), as amended,
would provide that the Department may, for good cause, accept
satisfactory experience obtained in a setting that would have been
eligible for registration but which has not registered with the
Department or experience that was obtained in good faith by the
applicant under the belief that appropriate authorization had been
obtained.

Section 14 of the bill would amend Chapter 420 of the Laws of 2002,
amending the Education Law in relation to social work, to (1) expand
the exemption from social work licensure requirements and from certain
corporate practice prohibitions so that the exemption would apply to
those employed in programs operated, regulated, funded, or approved by
a New York State or federal agency, political subdivision, municipal
corporation or local government agency or unit, and not just the
Department of Mental Hygiene or the Office Children and Family
Services, or specified local government units, (2) extend the
effectiveness of Chapter 420 to July 1, 2011 and (3) provide that the
Commissioner of Education will convene a workgroup of State agencies,
not-for-profit providers, professional associations and consumers, and
other key stakeholders to recommend by January 1, 2011 any amendments
to law, rule or regulation necessary to fully implement the
requirements for licensure by the new July 1, 2011 repeal date and
whether to extend beyond July 1, 2011 the authority of the Department
to register entities in accordance with Education Law §6503-a.

Section 15 of the bill would amend Chapter 676 of the Laws of 2002,
amending the Education Law in relation to psychology and mental health
practitioners to (1) extend the effectiveness of the exemption of
psychology from certain corporate practice prohibitions to July 1,
2011, which at such time it would be repealed (2) expand the exemption
from mental health practitioner license requirements and from certain
corporate practice prohibitions so that the exemption would apply to
those employed in programs operated, regulated, funded, or approved by
a New York State or federal agency, political subdivision, municipal
corporation or local government agency or unit and to provide for the
effectiveness of such exemption until July 1, 2011, at which time it
would be repealed, and (3) provide that the Commissioner of Education
convene a workgroup of State agencies, not-for-profit providers,
professional associations and consumers, and other key stakeholders to
recommend by January 1, 2011 any amendments to law, rule or
regulations necessary to fully implement the requirements for
licensure by the new repeal date of July 1, 2011 and whether to extend
beyond July 1, 2011 the authority of the Department to register
entities in accordance with Education Law §6503-a.

Section 16 of the bill is the effective date.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT OF THE BILL :

Chapters 420 and 676 of the Laws of 2002 established restricted
practice for the professions of licensed master social work, licensed
clinical social work, licensed mental health counseling, licensed
marriage and family therapy, licensed creative arts therapy, licensed
psychoanalysis, and licensed psychology, thereby making a range of
activities such as psychotherapy and certain types of counseling
subject to professional licensure requirements for the first time.
For decades prior to the enactment of Chapters 420 and 676,
not-for-profit corporations, education corporations, firms and
business corporations that are not professional business entities had
employed individuals to provide social work, psychotherapy and mental
health services. However, there are prohibitions against engaging in
corporate practice in these professions, and the new licensing law did
not provide a general recognition of such providers that employ
individuals licensed in these professions but who are not authorized
to do so under appropriate laws, such as the Mental Hygiene Law or
Article 28 of the Public Health Law.

Presently, the law restricts the practice of the professions of social
work and mental health practitioners and the provision of
psychotherapy services by professionals in medicine, nursing and
psychology to individuals or entities licensed by the Department.
Education Law §6512 makes it a Class E felony for an unlicensed person
to practice a licensed profession or hold oneself out as being able to
practice a licensed profession. Further, certain statutory provision&
relating to corporate practice generally prohibit the provision of
services by business corporations, not-for-profit corporations, or
non-licensee-owned entities. With certain exceptions, such as
speech-pathology and audiology, corporate practice (practice of a
profession by a corporation or other corporate entity) is generally
prohibited, with additional restrictions being applicable when
multiple professions are involved. Such practice must be conducted in
a legally authorized setting, such as a professional business entity,
an OMH clinic, or a Public Health Law Article 28 hospital, or in an
exempt setting. The law does not provide a general exemption or
recognition of community-based providers that employ individuals in
these professions, such as Riverside Mental Health or Samaritan
Counseling. Although some of these community providers fall within
existing statutory exemptions, others do not. Therefore, the
Department cannot accept the work experience gained in such settings
by applicants for licensure, and such experience cannot be applied
towards the qualifications for licensure of such applicants.  Nor can
the Department issue permits to individuals to practice in such
settings if they do not have the legal authority to provide· such
professional services.

Unless an exception to the restrictions on corporate practice is
provided, these entities could not continue to provide these
professional services without violating Title VIII of the Education
Law, and the Department could not accept experience gained by
practitioners employed by such entities for purposes of meeting
experience requirements for professional licensure.

To avoid the disruption of services that would result if these
entities could no longer deliver the professional services they have
been providing for many years, while assuring that the professional
services are subject to professional regulation for the protection of
the public, this bill would create an exception to corporate practice
in these professions and provide that non-professional business
entities, including not-for-profit corporations, education
corporations, firms, and business corporations, could continue to
deliver social work, psychotherapy and mental health services provided
that they obtain a registration from the Department by July 1, 2011.
Once registered, the entity would be subject to professional
regulation under Title VIII of the Education Law and would be
authorized to employ duly licensed professionals to provide such
services or to contract with professional business entities such as
professional corporations or professional limited liability companies
to deliver such services.
The bill would continue to recognize the authority of clinics and
programs authorized and regulated by certain public agencies,
including the Office of Mental Health (OMH), Office of Mental
Retardation and Developmental Disabilities (OMRDD), Office of Alcohol
and Substance Abuse Services (OASAS), and Department of Health (DOH).

This bill would address an omission in the law, which would otherwise
affect the ability of community-based providers not otherwise
authorized, to continue to employ licensed professionals to provide
professional services in these professions. Further, it would address
issues of qualifications of applicants for professional licensure so
that experience gained in registered settings may be applied towards
the experience qualifications for professional licensure. Thus, this
bill would maintain the status quo and allow such providers to
continue to deliver these services and allow· potential applicants for
licensure continue to gain their work experience in such
community-based settings.

 BUDGETARY IMPLICATIONS OF THIS BILL :

This bill should not result in significant costs to the State or local
governments. The bill would require business entities that provide
certain professional services to register with the Department under
new §6503-a and pay an initial registration fee of $400.00 and a
triennial registration fee of $150.00, which should defray costs
incurred by the Department in implementing the registration process
established in §6503-a.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act would take effect immediately.

provide for the effectiveness of such exemption until July 1, 2013, at
which time it would be repealed, (3) provide that on or before July 1,
2011, each exempted agency, local governmental unit and social services
district, either individually or on a group basis, submit to the Commis-
sioner of Education a report on the utilization of personnel subject to
the provisions in this bill (4) provide that the Commissioner of Educa-
tion will, after consultation with exempted state agencies, consumers
and other key stakeholders, submit a report to the Legislature by July
1, 2012 to recommend any amendments to law, rule or regulation necessary
to fully implement the requirements for licensure by July 1, 2013.
Section 15 of the bill is the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION: Chapters 420 and 676 of the Laws of 2002 established
restricted practice for the professions of licensed master social work,
licensed clinical social work, licensed mental health counseling,
licensed manage and family therapy, licensed creative arts therapy,
licensed psychoanalysis, and licensed psychology, thereby making a range
of activities such as psychotherapy and certain types of counseling
subject to professional licensure requirements for the first time.  For
decades prior to the enactment of Chapters 420 and 676, not-for-profit
corporations and education corporations, which are not professional
business entities, had employed individuals to provide social work,
psychotherapy and mental health services. However, there are prohibi-
tions against engaging in corporate practice in these professions, and
the new licensing law did not provide a general recognition of such
providers that employ individuals licensed in these professions but who
are not authorized to do so under appropriate laws, such as the Mental
Hygiene Law or Article 28 of the Public Health Law.

Presently, the law restricts the practice of the professions of social
work and mental health practitioners and the provision of psychotherapy
services by professionals in medicine, nursing and psychology to indi-
viduals or entities licensed by the Department.  Education Law §6512
makes it a Class E felony for an unlicensed person to practice a
licensed profession or hold oneself out as being able to practice a
licensed profession. Further, certain statutory provisions relating to
corporate practice generally prohibit the provision of services by not-
for-profit corporations. With certain exceptions, such as speech-pathol-
ogy and audiology, corporate practice (practice of a profession by a
corporation or other corporate entity) is generally prohibited, with
additional restrictions being applicable when multiple professions are
involved.  Such practice must be conducted in a legally authorized
setting, such as a professional entity, an OMH clinic, or a Public
Health Law Article 28 hospital, or in an exempt setting. The law does
not provide a general exemption or recognition of community-based
providers that employ individuals in these professions, such as River-
side Mental Health or Samaritan Counseling. Although some of these
community providers fall within existing statutory exemptions, others do
not.  Therefore, the Department cannot accept the work experience gained
in such settings by applicants for licensure and such experience cannot
be applied towards the qualifications for licensure of such applicants.

Nor can the Department issue permits to, individuals to practice in such
settings if they do not have the legal authority to provide such profes-
sional services.

Unless an exception to the restrictions on corporate practice is
provided, these entities could not continue to provide these profes-
sional services without violating Title VIII of the Education Law, and
the Department could not accept experience gained by practitioners
employed by such entities for purposes of meeting experience require-
ments for professional licensure.

To avoid the disruption of services that would result if these entities
could no longer deliver the professional services they have been provid-
ing for many years, while assuring that the professional services are
subject to professional regulation for the protection of the public,
this bill would create an exception to corporate practice in these
professions and provide that entities, including not-for-profit corpo-
rations and education corporations could continue to deliver social
work, psychotherapy and mental health services provided that they obtain
a waiver from the Department by July 1, 2012. Once an entity obtains a
waiver they would be subject to professional regulation under Title VIII
of the Education Law and would be authorized to employ duly licensed
professionals to provide such services or to contract with professional
business entities such as professional corporations or professional
limited liability companies to deliver such services.

The bill would continue to recognize the authority of clinics and
Programs, that operate under an operating certificate, by certain public
agencies, including the Office of Mental Health (OMH), Office of Mental
Retardation and Developmental Disabilities (OMRDD), Office of Alcohol
and Substance Abuse Services (OASAS), and Department of Health (DOH).

Finally this bill would extend the social work, mental health and
psychology licensure exemptions to certain state agencies and local
governmental units for three years (until July 1, 2013); require a work-
force study be completed by exempted state agencies and local govern-
mental units by July 1, 2011; and require the Commissioner of Education,
after consultation with state agencies, consumers and key stakeholders
to submit a report to the Legislature by July 1, 2012 to recommend any
amendments to law, rule or regulation necessary to fully implement the
requirements for licensure by July 1, 2013.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: 2009. - A.8897 - Ways & Means

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: To be determined.

EFFECTIVE DATE: This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Grants an exemption from licensing requirements for certain social work and mental health professionals employed by certain not-for-profit corporations, education corporations and business corporations if such corporations register with the education department; extends the expiration of provisions of law establishing licensing for social workers and mental health practitioners; directs the commissioner of education to convene working groups to study such provisions of law.
title: Grants an exemption from licensing requirements for certain social work and mental health professionals employed by certain corporations
